To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nonlinear image processing algorithms are not linear, that the frequency response of such algorithms is not constant, that the distortion properties of such algorithms are not constant, and that the imaging context of such algorithms affects the frequency response and distortion properties.
The nonlinear image processing algorithms used in digital image processing are nonlinear, and therefore have frequency response properties that are not well known, and that are not well understood.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel nonlinear image processing algorithm for the enhancement and restoration of images degraded by nonlinear processes.
the frequency response and distortion characteristics of nonlinear image processing techniques and their application to image enhancement and restoration in the presence of noise.
the development of a new class of algorithms for nonlinear image processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given image, the nonlinear processing method with the best frequency response will produce the best quality image.

the nonlinear image processing algorithms, such as the contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) algorithm, are not suitable for the analysis of the frequency response and distortion properties.
the frequency response of nonlinear image processing operations depends on the imaging context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nonlinear image processing algorithms are often nonlinear in their input and output, but not in their intermediate steps, and that the frequency response of the nonlinear algorithm can be approximated as the frequency response of an equivalent linear system.
the human visual system is a nonlinear, time-variant, adaptive system that is sensitive to the context in which the image is viewed and the task that is performed.
the frequency response and distortion properties for a wide range of image processing algorithms depend on the imaging context and the image processing algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nonlinear image processing algorithms can produce frequency response and distortion characteristics that are highly dependent on the image context.
nonlinear image processing algorithms can produce frequency response and distortion properties that are very different from those of linear algorithms.

the frequency response of nonlinear image processing (IP) algorithms is not a simple function of the frequency response of the underlying linear IP algorithms, but is also influenced by the distortion properties of the nonlinear IP algorithms.
